statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail holds at 25% on the floor of the elevated band and Stress is high at 70%.
recommendation: Nasdaq-100 futures are at 29,211, down 1.02% and 302 points, on a session range of 29,178.00-29,571.25. A marginal new low of 29,178.00 was made and rejected, leaving price about 33 points above it and a third consecutive hour without meaningful extension. The proximate trigger of the 08:00 UTC break is now verified: two very large crude carriers were struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz shortly after 08:00 UTC, an event distinct from the unverified Kharg Island image circulated a day earlier. The oil response is real but contained, with WTI at $87.70 and Brent at $91.95, and yields and volatility are flat against the previous hour. Tail therefore holds at 25% rather than easing, because the retracement remains shallow and the broken 29,435-29,570 band is unreclaimed, and rather than rising, because no leg has extended for three hours. Conditional risk stays concentrated in the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC window covering the US cash open and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases. The assessment would ease toward the WATCH band on a reclaim and hold of 29,330, and would move toward the strong-block band only on a decisive break below 29,178.00 followed by further extension or a verified disruption to Gulf export flows.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold 29,211 after a marginal new low at 29,178 is rejected, with verified Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes now identified as a driver of the 08:00 UTC break
body: The down-leg has now stalled for three hours and its cause has been identified. At 11:20 UTC Nasdaq-100 futures traded 29,208.50-29,211.00, about -1.02% and roughly 302 points below the 29,513 previous close, on a session range of 29,178.00-29,571.25. Two independent quote sources agree on the level and the range. Against the previous hour the session low was extended by only 6.25 points, to 29,178.00 from 29,184.25, that low was rejected, and price sits about 33 points above it. Price is roughly 12 points lower than the 29,223 print at 10:16 UTC, so the market has drifted rather than accelerated. The distinguishing development of this hour is evidential rather than structural. Reuters and Bloomberg both report, and maritime security consultant Marisks and the UK Maritime Trade Operations confirm, that two very large crude carriers were struck by unknown projectiles in quick succession while transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz shortly after 08:00 UTC. The Saudi-flagged Sidr, operated by Bahri, was hit about 16.6 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman, and the Liberian-flagged Senegal Prosperity, operated by Sinokor, was struck by three projectiles about 17 nautical miles east of the same point; each carried roughly two million barrels of Saudi crude and all crew are reported safe. This is a verified physical incident, materially different in character from the Kharg Island claim assessed a day earlier, which US military officials confirmed had not occurred and which rested on an AI-generated image. It is also the proximate trigger of the 08:00 UTC break through the overnight band, which had until now been attributed to the sovereign yield move alone. The transmission is nevertheless contained. WTI is $87.70, up 2.27%, and Brent $91.95, up 1.62%, each essentially unchanged against the levels seen an hour ago; the strait itself continues to function and no export flow disruption has been verified. The US 10-year yield is 4.78%, up about 2.5 basis points and still the highest since January 2025, with the 2-year at 4.36% and effectively unchanged on the day. VIX is 15.82, up 6.03% from a 14.43 close, within a 14.95-15.96 session range and therefore below its high and low in absolute terms. Shared cross-asset context collected at 10:50 UTC, roughly one hour old and within the freshness bound, shows complete coverage with Nasdaq futures at -0.89%, S&P at -0.49%, Dow at -0.43%, VIX at +1.15%, crude at +2.25% and gold at -1.08%, alongside uniformly negative megacaps, a mean change of -0.90% across the eight names, and semiconductors weaker still with Intel, Micron, Arm and AMD all down more than 1.5%. That context is delayed and latest-session, so it is used as cross-asset confirmation of a synchronised risk-off tone rather than as evidence of the current price path, and it confirms alignment without adding evidence of extension. Weighing this, Tail holds at 25%. It is not cut, because the bounce retraces only a small fraction of the decline, price remains in the lower part of a 393-point range, the 29,435-29,570 band is unreclaimed and the Hormuz threat is an unresolved mechanism capable of producing a second leg on any new headline. It is not raised, because the specific pathology that drove the 26% reading, repeated extension with price pinned to the low, has now been absent for three consecutive hours, oil has not extended, and the verified incident produced an orderly repricing rather than a gap-and-run. Stress rises one point to 70% on the confirmed physical escalation and the approaching data stack. Confidence is 87%, marginally higher than the previous hour, on two cross-verified futures quotes, verified yields, crude and volatility levels, a verified seven-day event calendar, a verified geopolitical incident confirmed by two independent outlets and two maritime sources, and fresh shared cross-asset context, moderated because tick-level retracement detail is not available.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Twenty-one of them mapped to the EA_ON band with Tail between 9 and 13 and Stress climbing steadily from 47 to 58, and dominant mode was mixed in 21 of the 24. Through the August 31 US session Stress rose as crude extended, the 10-year pushed to its highest level since January 2025 and September rate-hike odds firmed after the Jackson Hole address, while Tail stayed compressed because the price path itself remained two-sided. The overnight hours held that pattern with Stress at 50-58 and Tail at 9-11. The break came in the last three lookback hours on September 1: Tail 22 with mode trend-down at 08:00 UTC as the overnight band gave way, Tail 26 at 09:00 UTC as a second leg extended with price pinned near the session low, then Tail 25 at 10:00 UTC as that extension stopped. Today's verified Hormuz tanker strikes, timed shortly after 08:00 UTC, coincide with the start of that break and explain a shift previously attributed to the sovereign yield move alone.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is that today's combined rates and geopolitical repricing resolves into two-sided trade rather than a persistent no-retracement path, and the projection starts from a stalled leg rather than an accelerating one. Tail is therefore held at 25% through the European late morning, conditional on no new low. Conditional risk then concentrates in the 13:30-15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open, a Fed Barr appearance, the final S&P Global Manufacturing PMI and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases, where forecast Tail peaks at 28 and Stress at 76 with mode projected event/whipsaw, still below the strong-block threshold because event dispersion primarily raises Stress. The path is projected to decay from 16:00 UTC as post-release volatility ages, with a modest flow-driven uptick in the 19:00 UTC power hour around month-start rebalancing. Tail is projected back inside the EA_ON band from 20:00 UTC, reaching its trough near 03:00-04:00 UTC before firming gently with the Tokyo session and again into the September 2 European morning ahead of ADP. The projection would be invalidated by a decisive break below 29,178.00 followed by further extension, the index pinning to session lows through the US afternoon, another leg in the global bond rout, or a verified physical disruption to Gulf export flows rather than to individual vessels.
